marco_cs: Hi @olivia - quick check-in, we saw your integration create a lot of preflight tokens during the first hour and the gateway returned 429 intermittently. Can you share how your SDK is getting tokens?
olivia_customer: We mint ephemeral tokens per page load for security. We do ~10 parallel preflight requests on app init.
marco_cs: Got it. That pattern often triggers our preflight rate window. Two quick mitigation options: 1) reuse tokens across tabs for a short TTL, or 2) serialize preflight on the client with a single in-flight promise.
olivia_customer: Any config on Redwood side we can tweak while we change the client?
patrick_adops: We can temporarily bump the onboarding preflight rate for the account for 24h if you need a ramp. Ping me if you want that.
sylvia_eng: Also recommend adding jittered backoff on 429s and enable `connect: true` in the browser SDK so preflight handshake reuses the same underlying connection. Example snippet:
```
// single-flight preflight
if (!window._redwoodPreflight) {
  window._redwoodPreflight = fetch('/get-ephemeral-token')
}
return window._redwoodPreflight
```
olivia_customer: Ok we'll try single-flight. What's the TTL you recommend to share across tabs?
marco_cs: For onboarding, 1-2 minutes is usually fine. That keeps security strong but avoids stampedes. Also, if you can add a tiny client-side queue to cap concurrent preflights to 2, that's usually enough.
olivia_customer: Implementing now. If we still hit 429, we'll take Patrick up on the temporary bump.
deploy-bot: notice: account 0xA1 flagged for preflight-rate-increase-request by patrick_adops at 3541001400
patrick_adops: Request submitted, increased preflight window by 3x for 24h. Monitor logs and tell us if you see improvement.
marco_cs: One last tip — if you have a server-side token exchange (short-lived server-issued tokens), that can amortize preflight across clients and is best for high-traffic apps.
olivia_customer: Thanks team! Will report back in ~30m after rollout. :thumbsup:
